messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts observed on /v1/generate across us-west-2. Error rate spike started ~2160007600, current 5xx ~4.8% (baseline 0.2%). Paging maya_oncall and olivia_sre. Please ack and triage.
maya_oncall: acked. I'm on it — pulling dashboards. Do we have any ingestion of big prompt spikes or deploys? :eyes:
olivia_sre: no deploys in last 30m. Metrics show batching scheduler queue depth climbing; head-of-line blocking on some GPU pools (dedicated-pool-3). Latency for affected requests trending up then 504s. Suspect batcher saturation causing timeouts.
leo_prodeng: Confirming - traces show requests stuck waiting in scheduler queue > 5s before being batched. KV cache hit rates normal. Looks like a surge of many small concurrent requests that prevent efficient batching and create hol blocking.
samuel_infra: grabbing infra metrics now. `redis` batch queues show long tails: `redis-cli -h redis-main llen batch_queue:dedicated-pool-3` -> 1280. Node CPU on scheduler pods at 98%.
maya_oncall: ok immediate plan: 1) enable fallback route to smaller model variant for non-high-priority traffic 2) temporarily reduce max_batch_size to speed turnover 3) scale scheduler replicas 4) pause autoscaling on affected GPU pool to allow draining. Who can run the steps?
leo_prodeng: I can flip routing. Suggest we route 30% of production traffic for general requests to `redwood-ggml-small-v1` as a hot fallback.
olivia_sre: I'll change batcher params for `dedicated-pool-3` to `max_batch_size=8` and `batch_timeout_ms=30` to reduce head-of-line. Also enable `preemptive-eviction=true` on that pool. Pushing config now.
samuel_infra: scaling scheduler pods now: `kubectl -n infra scale deployment scheduler --replicas=6` — started. Watching pods come up.
infra-bot: Deployment scheduler scaled from 3 to 6 replicas by samuel_infra at 2160007812.
maya_oncall: after config push — seeing slight drop in queue depth (redis len -> 720). 5xx down to 2.9% but still elevated. Preparing routing change, @leo_prodeng please.
leo_prodeng: routing change applied (canary 30%). `POST /admin/route` ->
{ "route": "/v1/generate", "policy": "weighted", "weights": { "redwood-ggml-small-v1": 30, "redwood-rw-large-v1": 70 } }
Traffic validation shows 28% to small model. Observability shows latency tail for large model dropping slightly.
olivia_sre: batcher config applied on all scheduler pods in dedicated-pool-3. Logs show `batcher: max_batch_size=8 batch_timeout=30 preemptive_eviction=enabled`.
maya_oncall: good. What's customer impact now? tess_support, can you start notifying customers on the impacted list and draft a status update?
tess_support: on it. Pulling most-affected tenants from logs: top offenders by error-rate: AcmeCorp (5xx spike ~9%), PearlApps (6%), internal-integration 3rd-party connectors. Drafting message: "We're investigating elevated timeouts for text generation; we've applied mitigations and will follow up." Will post to affected customers after ops gives OOO.
leo_prodeng: quick check: `curl -s https://metrics.internal/api/series?m=rate(errors{path='/v1/generate',region='us-west-2'})` returns a 1m-rate consistent with drop from 4.8% -> 1.7% after changes. Still seeing intermittent 504s for long-context requests.
samuel_infra: I see scheduler pods still with high load on ordinal index 2. Killed one stale worker to force rebalance: `kubectl delete pod scheduler-2 -n infra` — new pod started. Should rebalance KV cache but that's fine for now.
olivia_sre: important note — bucketized traffic pattern: a flood of tiny requests (<50 tokens) is preventing batches from forming nicely for long requests, causing HOL for larger requests. Longer inputs queue waiting for smaller batches. Lowering max_batch_size alleviates lock but increases per-token overhead.
maya_oncall: decision log: continue current mitigations (canary routing, scaled scheduler, lower batch sizes, preemptive eviction). Ops to monitor 15m window. If 5xx > 2% for next 10m, escalate to exec and consider temporary rate-limit on free-tier.
incident-bot: NOTE — automated canary rollback watch scheduled: will alert if error rate on fallback model > 3%.
leo_prodeng: adding a temporary direct-serve path for high-priority customers to bypass batching entirely (`route=direct`) — will move AcmeCorp traffic to direct path while we stabilize.
infra-bot: Route change applied: AcmeCorp -> direct on dedicated-pool-3 by leo_prodeng at 2160007927.
maya_oncall: monitoring... 5xx now 1.1%, overall latency p50/p95 improved. However, a small subset of long-context requests still hitting timeouts (~2% of long-context). Is this acceptable short-term?
olivia_sre: I'd accept it short-term while we drain queues. Next steps for medium-term: tune batch scheduling algorithm to prioritize long-context requests after X ms waiting, and add starvation protection. I'll open an RFC for scheduler heuristics tomorrow.
samuel_infra: logs snippet showing what caused HOL:
2026-03-15T05:42:01Z scheduler[pid=12]: enqueued req=abc123 len=1024
2026-03-15T05:42:01Z scheduler[pid=12]: enqueued req=def456 len=12
2026-03-15T05:42:02Z batcher[pid=12]: created batch size=1 for req=abc123 (waiting for more small reqs)
2026-03-15T05:42:07Z batcher[pid=12]: timeout waiting for batch -> dispatching single large req
2026-03-15T05:42:12Z runtime[pid=55]: gpu kernel launch timeout -> 504 gateway
This pattern repeated; small requests starved larger ones because small reqs didn't coalesce quickly.
maya_oncall: status update to channel: mitigations in place, error rate trending down, partial customer impact controlled. Patching scheduler heuristics scheduled with priority tomorrow. Will handoff to night oncall in 30m. @tess_support — please send customer note now.
tess_support: customer note sent to affected tenants (AcmeCorp, PearlApps, third-party integrators). Support ticket created for each tenant with incident link and ETA for follow-up.
leo_prodeng: I'll monitor fallback model cost and performance — small model handles load fine. Suggest keeping 20% traffic on fallback for next 1h then ramp down if stable.
olivia_sre: kube autoscaler note: we temporarily disabled burst scaling to let queue drain; re-enable once queues under 100 and 5xx < 0.5%.
maya_oncall: current metrics at 2160008010: 5xx=0.9%, p95 latency down 30% from peak, redis batch_queue len -> 92. Taking notes for postmortem. Main root cause hypothesis: sudden surge of many tiny requests causing batching scheduler head-of-line blocking and GPU runtime timeouts for long-context jobs.
infra-bot: Reminder — create incident ticket in tracker and add runbook link: https://internal/incidents/runbooks/batching-hol
maya_oncall: creating ticket and adding initial timeline. Handoff to night shift @olivia_sre (on-call from 2160008055). Key actions for night: monitor 1h, allow gradual rollback of routing weights after 60m if stable, escalate if 5xx > 1.5% for 10m.
olivia_sre: ack handoff. I'll pick up and continue monitoring. Please include any debug artifacts in the incident ticket.
maya_oncall: thanks team — excellent run. Will add a short post-incident blameless note tomorrow with suggested fixes: scheduler starvation protection, dynamic batch-size per workload, and improved per-tenant routing controls. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE at 2160008055 — mitigations applied, service stabilized, incident moved to monitoring.
